extracted.intended_audience: Members of the public, stakeholders, regulated entities, small businesses, and local governments who want to submit comments on New York State proposed rules
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on how to find, time, and craft public comments on proposed New York State agency rules under the State Administrative Procedure Act (SAPA), including NY-specific strategic points to address in comments and procedural requirements to cite.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comment period length and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: The public has a minimum period of 60 days after publication to comment on a proposed rule (or if a hearing is required, the comment period extends to 5 days after the last public hearing).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure submissions are filed within the 60-day minimum; if a hearing is held, plan to submit within five days following the last public hearing to be considered timely.

rubrics_metrics.name: Where proposed rules are published / how to locate notices
rubrics_metrics.description: A Notice of Proposed Rule Making is published in the State Register. The Secretary of State publishes an electronic copy of the state register which is freely available on the internet.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the State Register (online electronic copy) to find Notices of Proposed Rule Making and the links provided there to agency contact/submission points.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methods of submitting comments (electronic links/email)
rubrics_metrics.description: When an agency provides an electronic mail address for the submission of comments, the Secretary of State provides a direct link between the electronic copy of the state register and that electronic mail address.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Typically submit comments electronically through the links provided in the State Register notice; follow the linked email/portal to ensure the agency receives your comment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability of SAPA to agencies and actions
rubrics_metrics.description: Most actions taken by state agencies are subject to SAPA requirements, though the Office of Court Administration and the Judiciary are exempt.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Confirm whether the agency/action is covered by SAPA before filing comments; note exemptions (Office of Court Administration and the Judiciary) where SAPA procedures do not apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Engage with the Regulatory Impact Statement (RIS)
rubrics_metrics.description: Engage with the Regulatory Impact Statement (RIS) the agency must publish.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Review the RIS closely and use it to challenge or support the agency's factual and economic assertions, assumptions, and conclusions about the rule's impacts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Address the Regulatory Flexibility Analysis for small businesses and local governments
rubrics_metrics.description: Address the Regulatory Flexibility Analysis for Small Businesses and Local Governments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether the analysis adequately considers impacts on small entities and local governments; supply data or examples showing disproportionate burdens or insufficient mitigation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Engage with the Job Impact Statement when displacement may occur
rubrics_metrics.description: Engage with the Job Impact Statement if the rule may displace workers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If job displacement is possible, comment on the adequacy of the Job Impact Statement, provide evidence of likely workforce impacts, and propose alternatives or mitigations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Note Rural Area Flexibility Analysis when applicable
rubrics_metrics.description: Note Rural Area Flexibility Analysis if applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify and document distinct rural impacts; argue for tailored analyses or accommodations when the rule affects rural communities differently than urban ones.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cite New York State law and prior agency guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Cite NY State law and prior agency guidance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Support legal and policy arguments by referencing relevant statutes, precedents, and previous agency guidance to show inconsistency, overreach, or legal error.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference SAPA Section 202 procedural requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Reference the SAPA Section 202 procedural requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Section 202 to challenge procedural shortcomings (e.g., inadequate notice, insufficient analyses) and to frame requests for corrective action or supplemental rulemaking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Demand that the Assessment of Public Comment in the final rulemaking address your points
rubrics_metrics.description: Demand the Assessment of Public Comment in the final rulemaking address your points.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Require the agency to explicitly respond to substantive comments in its final rulemaking record; ask for explanations of why the agency accepted or rejected specific arguments and evidence you raise.
